'''Vladimir Mikhailovich Lobashev''' ({{Langx|ru|Владимир Михайлович Лобашёв}}; July 29, 1934 – August 3, 2011) was a Soviet and Russian [[physicist]] and expert in [[nuclear physics]] and [[particle physics]]. He authored over 200 papers, of which 25 were considered groundbreaking.<ref name=INR1/>

==Early life and education==
Lobashev was born in [[Saint Petersburg|Leningrad]]. His father, Mikhail Yefimovich Lobashev, was a professor of [[physiology]] and [[genetics]] and head of the Department of Genetics at [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]].<ref name=INR1/>

Vladimir Lobashev graduated high school in 1952 with a silver medal. He earned a degree in physics at Leningrad State University in 1957.<ref name=INR1/> He defended his graduate thesis in 1963, and his doctoral thesis on the [[conservation law|non-conservation]] of spatial [[parity (physics)|parity]] in the [[gamma decay]] of [[atomic nucleus|nuclei]] in 1968.<ref name=INR1/>

==Career==
From 1957 to 1971, Lobashev worked as a laboratory assistant and as head of the [[Ioffe Institute|Ioffe Physical-Technical Institute]] in Leningrad, collaborating also with the Leningrad Institute of Nuclear Physics.<ref name=INR1/>

In 1972, Lobashev became head of the Department of Experimental Physics at the [[Institute for Nuclear Research]] in [[Moscow]].<ref name=INR1/>

In 1970, he was elected a corresponding member of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]]. He was awarded full membership in 2003.<ref name=INR1/>

==Research==
Lobashev's main areas of research were in [[Parity (physics)|P]] and [[CP violation|CP invariance]], and [[neutron]] and [[neutrino]] physics.<ref name=INR1/> He discovered a new effect in [[quantum electrodynamics]], the rotation of the plane of [[photon polarization|polarization]] of [[gamma ray]]s in the medium of polarized [[Electron|electrons]].<ref name=INR1/> His work on small effects of the non-conservation of spatial parity contributed to proving the universality of the [[weak interaction]], and earned Lobashev the [[Lenin Prize]] in 1974.<ref name=INR1/>

Lobashev found the most accurate limit then known on the [[electric dipole moment]] of the neutron, critical to the interpretation of [[CP violation]]. In experiments with polarized [[thermal neutron]]s, Lobashev demonstrated left-right asymmetry of [[nuclear fission|fission]] neutron capture.<ref name=INR1/>

With P.E. Spivakom, Lobashev proposed a new method for measuring the mass of the [[neutrino]]; this experiment placed a new lower limit on the mass of the electron antineutrino.<ref name=INR1/>

Lobashev, along with physicist [[Rashid Djilkibaev]], proposed the MELC experiment to search for [[lepton]] [[flavour (particle physics)|flavor violation]], which influenced the later [[Mu2e]] experiment at [[Fermilab]] in the US.<ref name=mustain/>

Lobashev was awarded the [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]] in 1984,<ref name=INR1/> the [[Bruno Pontecorvo Prize]] in 1998, the Markov prize in 2004, and the [[Humboldt Prize|Alexander von Humboldt Senior Researcher Award]].<ref name=fermilab/>
